headline: Mindanao Grid Placed on Yellow Alert as Power Reserves Tighten
seoTitle: Mindanao Grid Yellow Alert on August 11, 2026
seoDescription: NGCP placed the Mindanao grid under yellow alert as unavailable generating capacity tightened operating reserves. A yellow alert does not automatically mean rotational outages.
deck: NGCP placed the Mindanao grid under yellow alert Tuesday as unavailable generating capacity narrowed the system’s reserve margin.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: The National Grid Corporation of the Philippines placed the Mindanao grid under yellow alert on Tuesday, August 11, with the alert scheduled from 2 p.m. to 9 p.m., according to the GMA News report cited in the FMB News bulletin.

NGCP reported 2,672 megawatts of available capacity against projected peak demand of 2,527 MW, while 709.1 MW of generating capacity was unavailable. Those figures describe a tight reserve situation and should not be read as a declaration that blackouts are automatic.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: NGCP uses a yellow alert when the operating margin is insufficient to meet the transmission grid’s contingency requirement. It signals reduced room to absorb another major plant or system problem.

A yellow alert is different from a red alert and does not by itself mean rotational power interruptions will occur. Conditions can change as demand moves and generating units return to or leave service.

sections.heading: Why this matters to Filipinos
paragraphs: Thin power reserves can increase the grid’s vulnerability to another unexpected outage, affecting households, businesses and essential services across Mindanao if conditions deteriorate.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: Watch NGCP’s succeeding grid advisories for changes to the alert window, available capacity, demand and unavailable generation. Distribution utilities may also issue local notices if the system condition changes.
